question.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,0,-4⟩+t⟨2,4,3⟩,\,Π:4x+3y+4z-60=0.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨3+2t,4t,-4+3t⟩.
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+3y+4z-60 & =0 \\ 4x+3y+4z & =60 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,4⟩ & =60 \\ r\cdot ⟨4,3,4⟩ & =60\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+2t,4t,-4+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,3,4⟩ & =60 \\ ⟨3+2t,4t,-4+3t⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,4⟩ & =60 \\ 4(3+2t)+3(4t)+4(-4+3t) & =60 \\ 12+8t+12t-16+12t & =60 \\ 32t & =64 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+2(2),4(2),-4+3(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨7,8,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(7,8,2).$
